info.name: Lab 5: defence
info.description: One folder per grade, against the whole stack (docker compose up -d). Run folder 0 first: it creates the player and token the others use. After it, each folder runs on its own.

item.name: 0. Setup: a player and a token
Register a player

exec: pm.test('201: the player is created', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: Log in
Grade 4: Data Warehouse and ETL
The ETL job runs: its last run is ok

request.description: Asked through Grafana's Warehouse data source, so no database port or password is needed.

exec: const rows = (cols[0] || []).map((_, i) => Object.fromEntries(names.map((n, c) => [n, cols[c][i]])));
pm.test('it finished less than a minute ago', () => pm.expect(rows[0].age_seconds).to.be.below(60));

item.name: Extract + load: the new player reached dim_player

request.description: Player Service database -> stg_players -> dim_player. Repeats itself until the next ETL run has happened.

exec: const rows = (cols[0] || []).map((_, i) => Object.fromEntries(names.map((n, c) => [n, cols[c][i]])));
// the ETL job runs every 10 s: ask again, up to 8 times, until the row is there
pm.test('the player registered in Setup is in the warehouse', () => pm.expect(rows.length).to.equal(1));

pm.test('with its username, level 1 and 0 xp', () => { pm.expect(rows[0].username).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('user')); pm.expect(rows[0].level).to.equal(1); pm.expect(rows[0].xp).to.equal(0); });

item.name: Nothing private was copied: no password or email column

exec: const rows = (cols[0] || []).map((_, i) => Object.fromEntries(names.map((n, c) => [n, cols[c][i]])));
pm.test('none of them is a password or an email', () => pm.expect(columns.filter(c => /password|email/.test(c))).to.eql([]));

item.name: Create a session (a row for the Game side)

exec: pm.test('201: the session is created', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: Transform: the session reached fact_session, players counted

request.description: Game Service database -> stg_sessions + stg_members -> fact_session. `players` and `created_day` do not exist in the source: the transform derives them.

exec: const rows = (cols[0] || []).map((_, i) => Object.fromEntries(names.map((n, c) => [n, cols[c][i]])));
// the ETL job runs every 10 s: ask again, up to 8 times, until the row is there
pm.test('the session is in the warehouse', () => pm.expect(rows.length).to.equal(1));

pm.test('status active, 1 player (counted from the members), day column filled', () => { pm.expect(rows[0].status).to.equal('active'); pm.expect(rows[0].players).to.equal(1); pm.expect(rows[0].created_day).to.be.a('string'); });

item.name: Delete the session in the Game Service

exec: pm.test('204: gone from the Game Service', () => pm.response.to.have.status(204));

item.name: History: the deleted session is still in the warehouse

exec: const rows = (cols[0] || []).map((_, i) => Object.fromEntries(names.map((n, c) => [n, cols[c][i]])));

item.name: Grade 5: database replication and failover
Write: register a player (goes to the primary)

request.description: The Player Service has all three database nodes in its URL and keeps the one that accepts writes.

exec: pm.test('201: the write was accepted', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: Read it back through the service

exec: pm.test('200: the player is there', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Replicated: the row is on a replica (the ETL job reads replicas)

request.description: The ETL job connects with target_session_attrs=prefer-standby, so what it loads was read from a replica: the write made on the primary was streamed there.

exec: const rows = (cols[0] || []).map((_, i) => Object.fromEntries(names.map((n, c) => [n, cols[c][i]])));
// the ETL job runs every 10 s: ask again, up to 8 times, until the row is there
pm.test('the player came out of a replica into the warehouse', () => pm.expect(rows.length).to.equal(1));

item.name: Write to the Game database too: create a session

exec: pm.test('201: the write was accepted', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: Read it back, then clean up

request.description: Failover: `docker stop in-kahoots-with-the-undead-player-db-0-1` (or Test-Failover in lab5-tests.ps1), wait about 30 s, run this folder again: every request still passes, on the promoted node.

item.name: Grade 6: cache for common GET requests and for authentication data
A fresh player for this folder

request.description: Nobody has asked for this player yet, so the first GET below is certainly not in the cache.

exec: pm.test('201: the player is created', () => pm.response.to.have.status(201));

item.name: GET a player the first time: MISS, the Player Service answers

exec: pm.test('X-Cache-Node names the Redis node the key lives on', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Cache-Node')).to.match(/^cache-[0-9]+$/));

item.name: GET it again: HIT, answered by the gateway from Redis

request.description: The request never reached the broker or the Player Service: the gateway log says `-> cache at cache-N`.

exec: pm.test('from the same node as before', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Cache-Node')).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('cachedNode')));
pm.test('the same body the service gave', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('cachedBody')));

item.name: Change the player: the cached answer is dropped
GET after the change: MISS, and the new value

exec: pm.test('X-Cache: MISS (the change removed the key)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Cache')).to.equal('MISS'));
pm.test('the new display name, not the cached one', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().display_name).to.equal('Changed'));

item.name: The item catalog is cached too (asked twice: the second is a HIT)
A route that is not on the list is never cached

request.description: Only the GET routes in the gateway's CACHED_GETS list are cached: the ones whose answer is the same for every player.

item.name: Log in: a new token
Authentication data: the first request with a token verifies its signature (MISS)
The next request with it: the player id comes from Redis (HIT)

request.description: The key is auth:<SHA-256 of the token>, the value the player id. The token itself is never stored.

item.name: Logout needs a real token

exec: pm.test('401 for a token nobody issued', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: Log out: the token is revoked in the cache

request.description: A JWT cannot be taken back by the service that issued it. The gateway remembers it as revoked until it would have expired.

item.name: The logged out token is refused, although its signature is still valid

exec: pm.test('the reason is the logout', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().error.message).to.include('logged out'));

item.name: Another token of the same player still works

exec: pm.test('200: only the logged out token is refused', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: Grade 7: cache sharding by consistent hashing
30 keys are spread over the three nodes

request.description: Asks for /players/1 ... /players/30 (whether they exist does not matter) and counts the X-Cache-Node of each: the node the gateway's hash ring picked for the key get:/players/<n>.

exec: pm.test('every key names its node', () => pm.expect(Object.keys(nodes).every(n => /^cache-[0-9]+$/.test(n))).to.equal(true));
pm.test('all three nodes hold keys: ' + JSON.stringify(nodes), () => pm.expect(Object.keys(nodes).length).to.equal(3));

item.name: The same key always goes to the same node

request.description: The node is computed from the key alone (MD5 of the key, first ring point clockwise), so nothing has to be remembered about where a key is.

exec: pm.test('asked twice, the same node: ' + node, () => pm.expect(node).to.equal(first));

item.name: Different keys of one player may live on different nodes

request.description: A node going down, a node being added, and ring against `hash % N`: Test-CacheNodeDown and Show-HashRing in lab5-tests.ps1.

exec: pm.test('the inventory key has its own place on the ring', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('X-Cache-Node')).to.match(/^cache-[0-9]+$/));

item.name: Grades 8-9: saga for joining a session (it replaced the two phase commit)
A player who will join
A session to join
Join: one request, a saga of two steps in two services

request.description: The broker does not forward this request. It runs the saga join-session: step 1 sets the player online in the Player Service, step 2 seats the player in the Game Service. Each step commits in its own database at once.

exec: pm.test('the member the Game Service created', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().player_id).to.equal(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('joinerId'))));

item.name: The saga log: completed, both steps done

exec: pm.test('step 1 done on player (204), step 2 done on game (201)', () => pm.expect(steps).to.eql(['done 204', 'done 201']));
pm.test('step 1 kept what the flag was before: offline', () => pm.expect(saga.steps[0].kept.was_online).to.equal(false));

item.name: One saga by its id, with every step

exec: pm.test('the same saga, its payload and two steps', () => { const s = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(s.id).to.equal(pm.collectionVariables.get('sagaId')); pm.expect(s.payload.player_id).to.equal(Number(pm.collectionVariables.get('joinerId'))); pm.expect(s.steps.length).to.equal(2); });

item.name: Step 1 really happened: the joiner is online

request.description: Asked through the broker, as a service would: the gateway caches GET /players/{id} for 10 s.

item.name: Step 2 fails (already a member): 409, the answer of the Game Service
The saga log: compensated, step 1 was undone

exec: pm.test('step 2 failed with 409, step 1 compensated', () => pm.expect(steps).to.eql(['compensated 204', 'failed 409']));
pm.test('the reason is kept', () => pm.expect(saga.detail).to.include('failed on game: 409'));
pm.test('step 1 had kept: the player was already online', () => pm.expect(saga.steps[0].kept.was_online).to.equal(true));

item.name: The compensation put back the old value: the joiner is still online

request.description: Undo is not 'set offline': the player is seated from the first join. Step 1 kept what the flag was, and the compensation restored exactly that.

item.name: A player who was never online
Step 1 done, step 2 fails (no such session): 404

request.description: The Player Service had already committed online=true for this player when the Game Service refused. The coordinator runs the compensation of step 1.

exec: pm.test('404 from the Game Service', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

item.name: Compensated: the player is offline again
Step 1 fails (unknown player): 422, step 2 is never run
The saga log: step 1 failed, step 2 still pending, nothing to undo

exec: pm.test('step 1 failed with 404, step 2 pending', () => pm.expect(steps).to.eql(['failed 404', 'pending 0']));

item.name: The saga log needs the internal key
An unknown saga id: 404
The saga log is not on the gateway

exec: pm.test('404: players only see their own routes', () => pm.response.to.have.status(404));

item.name: Clean up: delete the session

request.description: The broker stopped in the middle of a saga, and the two phase commit this replaced: Test-SagaInterrupted in lab5-tests.ps1, and the commits named 'grade 8: two phase commit for joining a session'.
